name: James Patel
cvText:
James Patel
University of Bristol — BSc Economics, second year, predicted 2:1.
Education: studying corporate finance, statistics and microeconomics.
Campus Café — Part-time Team Member, September 2025–present.
Worked weekend shifts alongside university studies. Helped prioritise orders during busy periods and communicated delays to customers.
Economics group project — UK retail businesses, 2026.
Compared public annual reports for three UK retailers and helped present a summary of revenue trends. The current CV does not explain James’s individual conclusion or analytical method.
Bristol Economics Society — Member, 2025–present.
Attended talks about financial markets and career options.
Skills: Excel for basic tables and charts; PowerPoint presentations.
No banking internship, completed valuation model or evidenced leadership responsibility yet.

priorities.title: Make your analytical contribution clear
priorities.why: The retail project names the task but does not explain your method or conclusion.
priorities.action: Explain which measures you compared, what you found and the part you personally did.

priorities.title: Build technical foundations
priorities.why: The CV does not yet evidence a DCF or valuation project.
priorities.action: Learn enterprise versus equity value, practise a simple model and only add it once completed.

priorities.title: Make motivation specific
priorities.why: Interest in finance is visible, but there is no researched connection to a firm or team.
priorities.action: Choose one piece of the firm’s work and explain why it connects to your interests.

before: Compared public annual reports for three UK retailers and helped present a summary of revenue trends.
after: Compared revenue trends across three UK retailers using their public annual reports and helped present the group’s findings. [Add the measures you compared, your conclusion and your personal contribution.]
opening: I’m a second-year Economics student at the University of Bristol, working towards a 2:1. Alongside my studies, I work weekend shifts in a café, where I’ve learned to prioritise orders and communicate clearly under pressure. In a group project, I compared retailers’ annual reports and helped present revenue trends. That made me more interested in how businesses perform. [Add your own researched reason for this firm and role.]
application: Studying Economics at Bristol has developed my interest in how businesses perform and make investment decisions. In a university group project, I compared public annual reports for three UK retailers and helped present revenue trends. I would strengthen this example by explaining my own conclusion and method. Alongside my degree, weekend café work has taught me to prioritise orders and communicate delays during busy periods. I would bring that combination of analytical curiosity and practical teamwork to an internship. [Add a specific, researched reason for Goldman Sachs and the team you are applying to.]
